summary: Seed analysis is partial. The product targets guaranteed seed-determined item, loot, shop-stock, and reward spawns plus structural floor layouts; covered paths are tested against the pinned game, while some seed-determined spawn paths remain incomplete. Identities dependent on prior gameplay or Generator state, state-dependent shop details, and entity-rich maps are intentional non-goals.

implemented: Loop and FigureEight builders, including connection-room placement and pinned incremental collision-list order
Generic and region-specific standard-room geometry
Pinned standard, special, and secret room-count tables
Pinned SecretLarderRoom minimum dimensions and food-placement viability
Depth-1 lifecycle fixtures across ten seeds; full HKT-JZN-XQQ floor 6–8 parity; preserved-state AAA-AAA-AAA floor 2–4, 6–9, and 11 oracle fixtures
Oracle-backed fixed-form structural layouts for PrisonBossLevel, CityBossLevel, and LastLevel at depths 10, 20, and 26

Pinned SewerBossLevel generation at depth 5: exact room initialization, Goo landmark FigureEight retries and extra connections, all four Goo room painters, Rat King cache RNG, SewerPainter environment, doors, transitions, and layout-only normalization across five Java-oracle seeds

Pinned CavesBossLevel generation at depth 15: Java 23×23 elliptical arena, pylon patch placement and pathfinding retry lifecycle, entrance and corner variants, transitions, and normalized terrain/discoverability across four Java-oracle seeds

Pinned HallsBossLevel generation at depth 25: five variable chambers, statue/decor and water patches, center-piece terrain, pathfinding retry lifecycle, transitions, and normalized terrain/discoverability across four Java-oracle seeds

Depth-22 Halls lifecycle fixture: full prior-floor replay matches the Java pre-paint RNG checkpoint, room selection, and room bounds; HallsPainter includes REGION_DECO_ALT variance and unconnected-neighbour terrain merges
remaining: Coverage is fixture-specific; unrecorded builder histories can still diverge

Later regular floors still require phase-by-phase parity checks

Full SecretMaze layout plus covered Armory, Garden, Library, SecretLibrary, Pit, RotGarden, WeakFloor, DemonSpawner, Summoning, and ToxicGas paint behavior

implemented: Forced drops, generator decks (including pinned concrete-class undoDrop no-op semantics), main RegularLevel createItems drops, and supported special-room prizes
Item identities and exact heap capture on committed Java-oracle fixtures, including UnstableSpellbook constructor RNG

AAA-AAA-AAA Generator and heap parity: floor 6 weapon lifecycle from floor-3 SacrificeRoom through shop and createItems; floor 7's five main Generator drops; exact normalized heaps on floors 8–9, 12–14, and 16–19; floor 11 deterministic heaps, Mimic reward lifecycle, forced drops, CrystalKeys, and fresh-meta GuidePage placement. These remain internal Java-parity evidence

Supported quest rewards retain exact internal parity state, including both Wandmaker reward identities persisted through AAA-AAA-AAA floor 19; inherited population or Generator taint no longer hides a later independently selected quest, and public reports expose only reward-specific deterministic facts
Seed finder optional minimum item upgrade-level matching across the analyzed floor range for exact predictions only

SacrificeRoom reports preserve exact generation internally and expose a cursed weapon with pinned one-higher floor-set tier bounds (tiers 2–5 on depths 1–4, 3–5 on depths 6–14, and 4–5 on depths 16–24) plus a final +0..+3 upgrade range; concrete identity, enchantment, and map contents remain hidden

Regular createItems heaps and ordinary/Golden Mimic loot remain internal because persistent Generator history can change identity, heap kind, and placement. Public reports, exact search, heap/mob facts, and markers omit them; room-hosted Mimic cells remain independently reportable

Shop stock has internal pre-shuffle role provenance. Fixed and default-probability identities remain exact; persistent-deck weapon, missile, wand, and ring slots expose stable category/tier and forced level/curse constraints; the artifact-or-ring fallback omits its runtime-sensitive level; ChooseBag and Hourglass sand are conditional inventory-state facts

Public reports omit all FOR_SALE shop heap and marker cells because bag availability and Hourglass sand count change shuffle length and every stock position; constrained shop slots cannot satisfy exact searches

When a seeded rare-shop branch requests an Artifact, prior artifact exhaustion can force a Ring fallback whose constructor RNG changes the build and remaining floor stream. Public reports retain deterministic shop stock and label the uncertain slot as artifact or ring, but omit builder choice, room classes, static room facts, map, and post-ShopRoom item/quest facts; feeling, forced items, previously selected pending rewards, and other pre-callback quest selections remain reportable

Public shop entries use canonical report order, not the internal shuffle whose length and RNG path vary with bag, Hourglass, and artifact state; this reports spawn presence rather than stock placement

Ghost reporting keeps the exact armor class, shared reward level, weapon tier, and forced uncursed state while hiding the generator-history-sensitive weapon class and omitting enchantment/glyph outcomes

Wandmaker quest presence and type are selected during initRooms and remain public across later painter uncertainty. Reports render both distinct, uncursed choices concisely as +1…+3 wands without user-facing history warnings or concrete identities; duplicate-retry history suppresses later placed items and the spawn floor's public map because createItems can flatten grass

The Blacksmith's initial four-option pool retains exact default-probability identities, tiers, shared level, and uncursed state; enchantment/glyph outcomes are omitted, and later player-triggered pool regeneration is not predicted

BlacksmithRoom's two painted equipment rewards have separate provenance. Runtime-sensitive weapon/missile identities are constrained to category and tier; armor identity remains exact; Parchment-sensitive curse/enchantment/glyph properties are omitted. Cells, heap types, and markers remain internal with the regular-floor map

Imp reports render the reward as a concise +X ring with its stable post-two-upgrade level and forced curse, without a user-facing history warning or concrete ring identity. Isolated ring-deck selection and class-independent Ring.random calls preserve public room order and the later floor tail; the regular-floor map remains internal

Quest summaries preserve the seed-safe quest type/target prefix; Wandmaker uses the concise one of two +1…+3 wands label because prior wand history can change the final upgrade, and other quest reward-title suffixes use generic labels

The UI partitions ShopRoom stock and quest-provenance rewards into dedicated Shop and Quest rewards sections; those entries are not repeated under general floor items, and Blacksmith and Imp reward rows omit their redundant quest-source badges

Wandmaker choices persisted into later internal floor states for Java-oracle parity are explicitly internal-only and are not repeated publicly after the spawn floor, where the player may already have claimed one
Explicit Parchment Scrap state and pinned HKT-JZN-XQQ floor-13 Java-oracle parity evidence, retained as internal evidence rather than a public concrete prediction

Special-room rewards retain exact internal generation; public output uses painter-emitted static contracts rather than sampled items. This covers Study, Ritual, Ring, SuspiciousChest, and GrassyGrave center callbacks. Crypt exposes its floor-set armor distribution and forced curse; Statue exposes its forced-uncursed, positively enchanted weapon contract; audited families retain invariant source counts/categories while omitting unsafe fields and placements

Armory reports expose the guaranteed 2–3 base-reward count, without-replacement bomb/weapon/armor/missile category set, depth floor-set equipment tier bounds, +0..+2 upgrade bounds, tierless +0 uncursed bomb branch, Parchment-sensitive equipment curse/enchantment condition, and the separately conditional queued Trinket Catalyst

Legacy special-room summaries now retain source-backed reward structure: Library's first-scroll pair and 1–3 count; Treasury's 2–3 gold/Catalyst sources plus conditional six-pile heap branch; Storage and Magical Fire's 3–4 count and category fallback; Runestone's 2–3 stone/Catalyst precedence; Laboratory's fixed five-crystal stack plus 1–2 prize sources and meta-dependent pages; and Toxic Gas's doubled main gold plus two gold/Catalyst chests

Guaranteed limited-drop identities are reported as exact floor spawns and can satisfy seed-finder searches. Every regular floor has a food spawn; floor 1 reports its exact seed-determined identity and item name, while later floors retain a food-category constraint. Halls depths 21–24 have one aggregate constraint for two Torches; seeded Large feelings add a second food spawn. Even-count Scrolls of Upgrade retain their Forbidden Runes removal condition

SecretLibraryRoom retains exact private-pool base scroll identities and placement internally, with its JVM HashMap order pinned by a targeted Java oracle; public output exposes only 2–3 distinct scroll-base rewards and labels Exotic Crystals conversion as conditional

Runtime-sensitive population taint persists across later floors for dependent Generator-backed identities, layout, maps, and ordinary item tails. Because each floor's level RNG is freshly seeded, inherited taint alone does not suppress that floor's independently selected quest or invariant reward facts; a current-floor pre-quest divergence still hides its dependent quest tail
remaining: Loot tied to uncovered room paint or lifecycle paths can be incomplete or misplaced
Seed-determined spawn families on uncovered generation paths still require fixture-backed verification
areas.impact: A guaranteed seed-determined spawn or property can still be missing from the report on an uncovered generation path.

implemented: Structural room geometry, walls, traversable floor, door merge, graph painting, and entrances/exits for supported regular-floor paths
Profiled analysis captures a pre-population painter snapshot, from which the public contract projects structural layout only

A dedicated sequential layout projection prevents uncertain NPC, mob, heap, and item population from tainting later structural layouts. Internal callbacks still execute when their RNG or persistent Generator effects can change structure

Real-seed CXG-FJT-BFQ and HKT-JZN-XQQ references document intentional public map omission. A Playwright-only synthetic FloorMap exercises dialog, zoom, focus, responsive layout, and liquid animation without exposing unsafe production cells
Pinned gameplay references for HKT-JZN-XQQ floor 12 and its Troll Blacksmith MiningLevel branch, with the branch explicitly retained as source-only evidence
Fixture-backed terrain and render facts for selected special rooms
remaining: Uncovered room painters and later regular floors can produce incomplete structural geometry, doors, or transitions

Layouts whose builder, room set, or structural painter output can change with player state are not exact predictions; entity-only Generator, quest, inventory, and meta dependencies must not suppress an otherwise exact structural layout
Quest-branch levels, including the Troll Blacksmith MiningLevel reference, are not generated or rendered by the analyzer
areas.impact: Public previews show deterministic painter-complete floor layout, including terrain, traps, plants, and blobs captured before population. They intentionally make no claims about NPCs, mobs, heaps, item placement, or the final populated gameplay map.

implemented: Deterministic seeded generation needed by the regular-floor analyzer
remaining: The unseeded early Guidebook page is intentionally excluded
Player decisions and inventory changes are not inferred
Concrete identities and properties that depend on prior gameplay or persistent Generator history are intentionally ignored; independently seed-determined constraints are retained

Concrete quest and special-room reward identities or equipment properties affected by player state, artifact history, Generator history, or player-triggered regeneration are intentionally excluded; proven invariant categories, counts, tiers, levels, curse states, and alternatives remain reportable
Shop identities, conditions, order, and placement that depend on artifact exhaustion, bag availability, Hourglass state, persistent decks, inventory state, or JVM iteration are intentionally excluded
Item, shop-stock, and reward placement cells are intentionally excluded; the public claim is guaranteed spawn presence and seed-determined properties
Entity-rich maps are intentionally excluded: public maps contain structural layout only, without items, mobs, traps, plants, blobs, decoration, or loot placement
Full parity claims remain blocked until the overall status is explicitly promoted from partial
areas.impact: These inputs or behaviors are not predictions and should not be interpreted as analyzer errors.
